Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address City Council on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other matter
within its jurisdiction subject to the rules of decorum described in Section 2.08.020 of the Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to
address City Council, please complete a speaker card and hand the card to the Sergeant at Arms. City Council will hear public
comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote and on matters not listed on the
agenda during the Oral Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain
emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for
consideration at a future City Council meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the City Council: Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less
and
directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City meeting or
other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk’s department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening devices are
available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the
agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability. Notification of at least 48
hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements
can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it has
been posted will also be made available for public inspection. Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City
Clerk’s Department, during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday – Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every
other Friday; telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e-mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

The City Attorney indicated there was no reportable action taken on the matters discussed
in closed session.

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

Councilmember Perez thanked all residents for being active within the community from
reporting issues to expressing appreciation. Councilmember Ramirez reported on his
attendance at Troy and Bob’s Auto Works 80th Anniversary and reminded residents to be
mindful of pedestrians as the new school year begins. Councilmember Valencia wished
children a great school year; reported on her attendance at Troy and Bob’s 80th
Anniversary and the Summer Concert; and shared that a Health Fair, in partnership with
Supervisor Janice Hanh, will be held September 14 at City Hall. Mayor Rios welcomed
dignitaries in attendance; encouraged residents to check on their elderly neighbors during
the heat wave; reported on her attendance at Coffee with a Quadrant Officer at
McDonalds, and the Pack to School event; invited all to attend upcoming events:
Community Listening Session August 22, at the Senior Center and Meet the Mayor for
Palletas Y Platicas August 26, at La Michoacana on Pioneer Boulevard.

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

City Council presented a proclamation declaring August as National Wellness Month in
the City of Norwalk, accepted by Maria ^^, Manager, LA Care Community Resource
Center.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

Mr. Gomez indicated that the Senior Center is a cooling center and in the near future
Faith Church will be as well. The Sheriff’s Department quarterly report update was
provided by Captain Conti; City Council congratulated Captain Conti on being recognized
as a top leader in the Sheriff’s Department for Los Angeles County and his one-year
anniversary as Captain. Mr. Gomez provided a Firestone Bridge Widening update and
shared that there is a lot of construction and encouraged residents to be cautious and
considerate. Videos were shared highlighting Senior Center Lobby Olympics, National
Night Out, and Bi-Weekly Review.

SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION NO. 24-48 - APPROVAL OF AN APPLICATION FOR GRANT

  EXPANSION

Background:

On November 8, 2016, Los Angeles County voters approved the Safe, Clean Neighborhood
Parks, Open Space Beaches, Rivers Protection, and Water Conservation Measure (Measure
A). This measure created several funding opportunities and programs. Among them was the
Acquisition-Only Competitive Grant Program (RPOSD grant) administered by the Los Angeles
County Regional Park and Open Space District (the District). The RPOSD grant aims to increase
parkland acreage totals through the acquisition of land for new parks and expansion of existing
parks.

The City has been engaged in a decades-long process to purchase land owned by the U.S. Air
Force (Air Force) and once used as a tank farm located next to Holifield Park at Excelsior Drive
and Norwalk Boulevard. Norwalk was deeded 15-acres of the property in August 2016. Since
then, the land has been going through a remediation process. The Air Force is overseeing
remediation on the remaining 36-acres. The City’s intent is to acquire the remaining 36-acres
and develop the entire parcel into a regional park. As the Air Force has stated an intention to
sell the remaining acres at or close to full market value, the City needs to prepare funds for the
purchase. This grant is specifically for the purchase of land for park purposes. The maximum
that can and will be requested is $2,000,000.

Fiscal Impact:

The City engaged California Consulting, one of the top grant writing firms in the state, to prepare
the RPOSD grant application for $12,000. This amount was budgeted in the Fiscal Year 2024/25
budget and will be paid with General Fund monies.
 City Council  September 3, 2024
Resolution No. 24-48 – Approval to Apply to RPOSD Grant  Page No. 2

If awarded the full requested amount, the City can expect to receive $2,000,000 to help fund the
purchase of the remaining 36-acres. There is no match requirement, though the City will likely
need further funding for the purchase.

Resilient and Economically Prosperous City; Complete the expansion of Holifield Park.

Recommended Action:

COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK APPROVING THE FILING OF AN APPLICATION FOR
GRANT FUNDS FROM THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY REGIONAL PARK AND OPEN SPACE
DISTRICT FOR MEASURE A FUNDING FOR THE HOLIFIELD PARK EXPANSION.

Background:

On August 6, 2024, City Council adopted Urgency Ordinance No. 24-1752U, a 45-day
moratorium to establish, implement, or operate (temporarily or permanently) convenience stores
(liquor stores), discount stores, personal use – laundromat, vehicle/automobile washing, payday
loan establishments, emergency shelters, single-room occupancy, supportive housing, and
transitional housing city-wide (Attachment No. 1).

Per Government Code Section 65858(d), ten days prior to the expiration of that interim ordinance
or any extension, the legislative body shall issue a written report describing the measures taken
to alleviate the condition which led to the adoption of the ordinance.

Discussion

Urgency Ordinance No. 24-1752U, which is valid for 45 days, is set to expire on September 20,
2024, unless extended by City Council. After notice pursuant to Government Code Section
65090 and public hearing, Government Code Section 65858(a) states that City Council may
subsequently extend the ordinance for 10 months and 15 days. Further, the urgency ordinance
may be subsequently extended for one additional year. No more than two extensions may be
adopted.
 City Council  September 3, 2024
10-Day Report - Urgency Ordinance No. 24-1752U  Page No. 2

Analysis

Since the City’s adoption of Urgency Ordinance No. 24-1752U, staff began research to
determine and quantify the impacts of convenience stores (liquor stores), discount stores,
personal use – laundromat, vehicle/automobile washing, payday loan establishments,
emergency shelters, single-room occupancy, supportive housing, and transitional housing city-
wide.

Specifically, staff has started the following research:

  1. Reviewed City business license records to quantify the number of each type of use
  operating within the City;
  2. Initiated studies of land use tables for surrounding cities for the same or similar uses to
  determine if the uses are permitted by right, not permitted or permitted with a discretionary
  review (such as a conditional use permit);
